There are no visual highlights such as shading, thick outlines, or additional annotations on specific bars.

model_annotations.English: Figure 5 presents a bar chart comparing per-output and per-layer perplexity at different sparsity rates, using a logarithmic scale for perplexity to accommodate the wide range of values. The horizontal axis represents sparsity rates, labeled at intervals of 10% from 10% to 80%, and the bars are arranged in ascending order of sparsity rate. The vertical axis is labeled "Perplexity" and uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 10¹ to 10³, with tick marks at 10¹, 10², and 10³. Each sparsity rate has two adjacent bars: blue for "Per-Output" and orange for "Per-Layer", as indicated in the legend. At lower sparsity rates (10% to 50%), both methods yield similar perplexity values, with the blue bars (Per-Output) slightly taller than the orange bars (Per-Layer) in most cases. As sparsity increases to 60%, the bars remain relatively close in height, with Per-Output at approximately 10¹ and Per-Layer slightly lower. At 70% sparsity, the Per-Output bar reaches approximately 10², while the Per-Layer bar is slightly lower. At 80% sparsity, the Per-Output bar reaches approximately 10².5, and the Per-Layer bar is slightly higher, reaching approximately 10².7. The chart visually demonstrates that both methods maintain low perplexity at lower sparsity rates, but the performance gap widens at higher sparsity rates, with Per-Layer showing higher perplexity than Per-Output at 80%. The figure caption notes that the logarithmic scale is used due to the significant difference in values between high and low sparsity rates.
